title: Quadratic Regression Moving Average (QRMA)
summary: Fits a parabola to the last N prices by least squares and plots the fitted value at the newest bar, so the line follows curvature as well as slope.
descriptionHtml:
The Quadratic Regression Moving Average fits the curve y = a + b x + c x^2 to the source over the last period bars, with x = 0 at the oldest bar of the window and x = period - 1 at the newest. The fit is ordinary least squares: the three normal equations are solved with Cramer's rule, using sums of x up to the fourth power that depend only on the period.

The value plotted is the fitted curve at the newest bar. A straight-line fit can only follow a slope; adding the squared term lets the line bend with a move that is speeding up or slowing down. Until period bars exist the line shows the price itself, and a missing price counts as zero.
howToReadHtml:
Read it as a fast trend line. Because it fits curvature, it stays close to price through accelerating moves and turns sooner than a simple or linear average of the same length. Price above a rising line describes an uptrend, and below a falling line a downtrend.

The same flexibility is its limit: at the end of the window a parabola can overshoot, so after a sharp reversal the line may briefly run past price. Shorter periods make it react faster and more nervously; longer ones steady it.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many bars the parabola is fitted to. At least 3, since a parabola needs three points.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series the curve is fitted to, the close by default.

faq.q: How is it different from a linear regression average?
faq.html: A linear fit draws a straight line through the window, so it lags whenever the move curves. The quadratic fit adds a bend and keeps up with a move that is accelerating or fading.
The parabola is read at the very end of the window, where a curve fitted to the past is least constrained. After a sharp turn it can extend the old curvature for a few bars.

faq.q: Why must the period be at least 3?
faq.html: A parabola has three unknowns, so it needs at least three bars to be fitted.

related.title: Rainbow Moving Average (RAIN)
related.summary: Ten simple averages stacked on top of each other and blended back into one line, with the faster layers weighted most.

related.title: Quadruple EMA (QEMA)
related.summary: Four chained exponential stages with rising smoothing factors, combined 4, -6, 4, -1 to cancel most of the lag of an ordinary EMA.

related.title: Regularized EMA (REMA)
related.summary: An exponential average blended with a regularization term by a lambda setting, which in this form slows the step by alpha times lambda.
